steps.prompt:
Use FAST to check for stroke signs:

Face — Ask them to smile. Does one side droop?
Arms — Ask them to raise both arms. Does one drift down?
Speech — Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is it slurred or strange?
Time — If any of these are present, call emergency services immediately.
Call emergency services immediately. Note the exact time symptoms started — this is critical for treatment decisions. Do not give the person anything to eat or drink.

Help the person sit or lie in a comfortable position. If conscious: support the head and upper body slightly raised. If unconscious but breathing: place in recovery position on their weaker side. Do not leave them alone.
Do not give aspirin or any medication — this can cause harm if the stroke is caused by bleeding rather than a clot. Monitor breathing and responsiveness until emergency services arrive.
steps.cta: Note symptom time and await emergency services — do not give medication

steps.prompt: FAST is the primary stroke check. Other symptoms may include: sudden severe headache with no known cause, sudden vision loss in one eye, sudden severe dizziness or loss of balance. If these are sudden and severe, call emergency services.
steps.cta: When in doubt, call emergency services — sudden neurological symptoms need urgent review
